name: Homemade Corn Tortillas
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
steps: In a large bowl, stir together the masa and salt.
Add the water, and mix together well to form a dough.
Turn out onto a lightly floured board and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into ¼ cup (3 oz / 90 g) portions, and form them into balls.
Roll each ball into a flat round about 6 inches (10 cm) in diameter and ⅛ inches (0.25 cm) thick.
Heat a large heavy skillet over medium high heat.
Place the tortillas one at a time into the dry hot skillet; cook until brown on one side, then turn and brown the other side.
Remove from the skillet and keep warm in cloth towel.

culture.text: A tortilla is a thin, circular unleavened flatbread, originally made from corn (maize) but now also made of wheat flour. The corn tortilla is a staple food in most of Mexico and Central America, while the flour tortilla is typical of Northern Mexican and Mexican-American cuisine. The tortilla has become popular across the world.
